headline: Denmark is due to introduce a bill banning the sharing of realistic AI deepfakes of people without their consent.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: the full Euronews text supports the headline; the bill has not passed.
importance_line: What changed: a bill due on 8 Oct 2026 would make it unlawful to share realistic AI copies of a person's face or voice without consent, while still allowing satire and criticism. Ordinary people and artists would be protected, but the bill has not passed yet.
summary: Euronews reports that Denmark is due to introduce a bill that would ban sharing realistic AI deepfakes of people's faces and voices without their consent, as an amendment to its copyright law. Culture minister Zenia Stampe says the main goal is to get tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly.
notes: Pool item is The Daily Star (one paragraph read; origin of its text not stated); Euronews read in full and used as the source. Chosen category LAW; chunk default POL or LAW.
